# SQRTOJ Modern Competitive-Programming Design System

This directory contains the specification, requirements, technical design, and
task breakdown for the **Modern Competitive-Programming (MCP)** UI overhaul of
SQRTOJ.

The goal is a clean, content-dense, token-driven flat design that keeps the
information density a judge needs (scoreboards, submission tables, verdicts,
problem lists) while modernizing the look, unifying the color system, and making
dark mode a first-class, instantly switchable feature.

## Reading order

| # | Document | What it covers |
|---|----------|----------------|
| 1 | [`01-vision-and-principles.md`](01-vision-and-principles.md) | The design philosophy, target users, and the principles every decision is measured against. |
| 2 | [`02-requirements.md`](02-requirements.md) | Functional and non-functional requirements, scope, and acceptance criteria. |
| 3 | [`03-design-tokens.md`](03-design-tokens.md) | The token layer: color scales, typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion. The single source of visual truth. |
| 4 | [`04-technical-design.md`](04-technical-design.md) | How the system is implemented in the existing SCSS + `django_jinja` + `django_compressor` pipeline, theming architecture, and migration strategy. |
| 5 | [`05-component-specs.md`](05-component-specs.md) | Per-component visual and behavioral specs (navbar, buttons, tables, badges, forms, etc.). |
| 6 | [`06-implementation-roadmap.md`](06-implementation-roadmap.md) | Phased, checkbox task list with dependencies and estimates. |
| 7 | [`07-accessibility.md`](07-accessibility.md) | Contrast, focus, motion, and semantics requirements plus a verification checklist. |

## Current state (baseline)

Grounded in the repository as of this writing:

- **Styles** live in `resources/*.scss`, aggregated by `resources/style.scss`, and
  built into `style.css` (light) and `dark/style.css` (dark) by `make_style.sh`.
- **Theme values** are duplicated across `resources/vars-default.scss` (light) and
  `resources/vars-dark.scss` (dark), with shared tokens in
  `resources/vars-common.scss`. Both `@forward "vars-common"`.
- **Theme selection** is driven by `Profile.site_theme` (`auto` / `light` / `dark`,
  see `judge/models/choices.py`), surfaced to templates by
  `judge.template_context.site_theme`, and mapped to files via
  `DMOJ_THEME_CSS` in `dmoj/settings.py`. `templates/base.html` links the light
  and/or dark stylesheet, currently gated behind the `judge.test_site` permission.
- **Brand color** is a hardcoded green (`#045c20`) in `resources/navbar.scss`; the
  navigation bar background is set inline in `templates/base.html` (`#231F20`).
- **Link palette** is a separate blue scale, unrelated to the green brand color.
- **Typography** relies on system fonts (`Segoe UI`, `Lucida Grande`, `Arial`) with
  `Source Sans Pro` for the navbar; monospace uses a long fallback stack in
  `resources/vars-common.scss`.
- **Blog** already has a modern, well-considered token set (`$color_blog_*` in the
  `vars-*.scss` files) that is siloed to that feature. The MCP system generalizes
  that direction to the whole site.

## Non-goals

- No markup rewrite of every template in one pass. The rollout is incremental and
  ships value at each phase.
- No new frontend framework (no React/Vue/build-tool swap). We stay on
  server-rendered templates + SCSS + `django_compressor`.
- No change to the judging, contest, or submission *logic*. This is presentation
  only.
- No visual trend that harms readability (glassmorphism, neumorphism) — see
  `01-vision-and-principles.md`.

## How to contribute to this effort

Follow the conventions in the repository root `AGENTS.md`: match existing
DMOJ/VNOJ patterns, keep changes minimal and focused, run `flake8` for Python and
`npm run format:check` for websocket JS, and build styles with `./make_style.sh`
before finishing frontend work.

```

# 02 — Requirements

Requirements use `MUST` / `SHOULD` / `MAY` per RFC 2119. Each has a stable ID so
tasks (`06-implementation-roadmap.md`) and tests can reference it.

## 1. Functional requirements

### FR-1 — Design token layer
- **FR-1.1** The system MUST expose a single set of design tokens (color, spacing,
  radius, elevation, typography, motion) as the source of truth for all styling.
- **FR-1.2** Tokens MUST be emitted as CSS custom properties on a root scope so they
  are available to every stylesheet and to runtime.
- **FR-1.3** Every token MUST have a value in both the light and dark themes.
- **FR-1.4** Component and page styles MUST reference tokens rather than literal
  color/spacing values, except for values that are intrinsically fixed (e.g. `0`,
  `100%`, `1px` hairlines where a token is not meaningful).

### FR-2 — Theming
- **FR-2.1** The site MUST support at least three theme modes, preserving the
  existing `SITE_THEMES` choices: `auto` (follow system), `light`, and `dark`.
- **FR-2.2** `auto` MUST resolve via `prefers-color-scheme` without a server round
  trip.
- **FR-2.3** A logged-in user's saved `site_theme` MUST take precedence over the
  system preference, matching current behavior.
- **FR-2.4** Theme resolution MUST NOT cause a flash of the wrong theme (FOUC/FOWT)
  on first paint.
- **FR-2.5** The impersonation navbar override (purple bar) MUST continue to work.

### FR-3 — Core primitives
The following primitives MUST be redesigned against the token layer and documented
in `05-component-specs.md`: color/link styles, buttons, form controls, cards,
tables, badges/pills (including verdict and rating variants), tabs, pagination,
alerts/messages, and the navbar.

### FR-4 — High-traffic pages
The following pages MUST be restyled using only the new primitives and tokens:
home, problem list, problem statement, submission list, submission detail, contest
list, scoreboard/ranking, and user profile.

### FR-5 — Verdict and rating semantics
- **FR-5.1** Submission verdicts (AC, WA, TLE, MLE, RTE, CE, IR, etc.) MUST have a
  dedicated, consistent visual treatment derived from tokens.
- **FR-5.2** Rating tiers MUST map to named tokens (newbie … grandmaster) rather
  than scattered literals.
- **FR-5.3** Where color conveys meaning (verdict, rating, contest status), a
  non-color cue (label, icon, or shape) MUST also be present.

### FR-6 — Typography
- **FR-6.1** The system MUST define a UI font stack, a monospace stack (for code),
  and a documented type scale (sizes + line-heights).
- **FR-6.2** Web fonts, if used, MUST load progressively (system font first, no
  render-blocking) and MUST NOT break math (MathJax) or code highlighting layout.

## 2. Non-functional requirements

### NFR-1 — Accessibility
- **NFR-1.1** Body text and meaningful UI text MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast
  (≥ 4.5:1; ≥ 3:1 for large text) in both themes.
- **NFR-1.2** All interactive elements MUST have a visible, token-defined focus
  indicator.
- **NFR-1.3** Motion MUST respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- **NFR-1.4** Interactive controls MUST preserve semantic HTML and keyboard
  operability; restyling MUST NOT remove focusability or semantics.

### NFR-2 — Performance
- **NFR-2.1** The redesign MUST NOT introduce render-blocking resources beyond what
  exists today; the token layer adds no extra network request (it ships inside the
  existing compressed CSS bundle).
- **NFR-2.2** Compiled CSS size growth SHOULD stay modest; net additions beyond a
  small budget SHOULD be justified in the phase that introduces them.
- **NFR-2.3** Theme switching MUST NOT require re-downloading a separate full
  stylesheet per theme once the token model is adopted (long-term target;
  see `04-technical-design.md` for the migration path).

### NFR-3 — Compatibility
- **NFR-3.1** The build MUST continue to work through `./make_style.sh`
  (`sass` + `postcss`/autoprefixer) and honor `.browserslistrc`.
- **NFR-3.2** Both `style.css` (light/default) and `dark/style.css` MUST continue to
  be produced so `DMOJ_THEME_CSS` mappings remain valid during migration.
- **NFR-3.3** Changes MUST NOT break `django-compressor` CSS/JS compression in
  `base.html`.

### NFR-4 — Maintainability
- **NFR-4.1** Token and component definitions MUST live in clearly named partials
  with a documented import order.
- **NFR-4.2** New styles MUST follow existing SCSS conventions in `resources/` and
  pass the project's frontend checks.
- **NFR-4.3** The documentation set MUST be kept in sync when tokens or component
  contracts change.

### NFR-5 — Internationalization
- **NFR-5.1** All new user-facing strings introduced by UI work MUST be wrapped for
  translation (`gettext_lazy as _`).
- **NFR-5.2** Layouts MUST tolerate longer translated strings (e.g. Vietnamese)
  without breaking (no fixed-width text containers that clip).

## 3. Constraints

- **C-1** Django 3.2 templates with `django_jinja`; no frontend framework is being
  introduced.
- **C-2** SCSS compiled by `sass`, post-processed by `postcss`/autoprefixer; this
  pipeline stays.
- **C-3** Theme selection persists on `Profile.site_theme` with values from
  `SITE_THEMES`; the data model for theming is not being changed by the UI work
  itself (any change requires a migration and is called out explicitly).
- **C-4** `dmoj/local_settings.py` is user-owned and git-ignored; defaults live in
  `dmoj/settings.py`.
- **C-5** Vendored widgets (`martor/`, `django_ace/`) and third-party CSS
  (select2, fontawesome) are integrated but not rewritten; the system themes them
  via tokens where feasible.

## 4. Out of scope (for this initiative)

- Rewriting JavaScript behavior or introducing a SPA/framework.
- Changing backend data models, APIs, or business logic.
- Redesigning the Django admin (`wpadmin`) internals beyond token-level theming.
- Content/IA changes (which pages exist, navigation structure) beyond visual
  restyling.
- Replacing MathJax, Ace, Pygments, or select2.

## 5. Assumptions

- The existing `test_site` permission gate for experimental theming can be used to
  roll out the new system to staff before general release.
- `prefers-color-scheme` support in target browsers (per `.browserslistrc`) is
  sufficient for `auto` mode.
- Design decisions can be validated on the live-representative templates already in
  `templates/` without new fixtures.

## 6. Acceptance criteria (initiative-level)

The initiative is accepted when:

1. All `MUST` functional requirements (FR) are implemented for the primitives
   (FR-3) and high-traffic pages (FR-4).
2. All `MUST` non-functional requirements (NFR) are verified per
   `07-accessibility.md` and the validation steps in `06-implementation-roadmap.md`.
3. `./make_style.sh` builds both themes cleanly and `python manage.py test judge`
   passes.
4. The documentation set reflects the shipped tokens and components.

```

## User

I do have some custom artworks that i want to insert, and i want the website to be in autumn style. what artworks should I do, and what is the color pattern?

## Assistant

Good direction — autumn suits an online judge well because warm, muted earth tones are low-eye-strain for long contest sessions. The key constraint: autumn is a *warm* palette, but your verdict colors (AC green, WA red, TLE amber) and rating tiers must stay functional and distinct. So the trick is to make **autumn the brand/surface layer** and kep **status colors as a separate, protected semantic layer**. Let me lay out both the palette and the artwork.

## Color palette

Autumn breaks into three sub-mods. I'd pick one as your primary identity:

| Mood | Fel | Best if |
|---|---|---|
| **Warm harvest** (my recommendation) | Amber, rust, gold, warm brown | You want cozy but still readable and professional |
| Dep maple | Crimson, burnt orange, oxblood | You want bold and dramatic (riskier for contrast) |
| Muted wodland | Olive, ochre, moss, taupe | You want calm and understated |

### Recommended tokens — "Warm Harvest"

Light theme (surfaces stay near-white so tables remain readable; warmth comes from accents and subtle tints):

```
--accent-500:  #C1440E   // burnt sienna — primary brand (navbar, buttons, links)
--accent-600:  #9E3609   // hover/active
--accent-300:  #E07B39   // pumpkin — highlights
--gold:        #E0A82E   // amber gold — secondary accent, badges
--page-bg:     #FBF6EF   // warm off-white (paper), NOT pure white
--surface:     #FFFFFF   // cards
--surface-alt: #F4EBDD   // subtle warm tint for zebra rows / panels
--border:      #E4D5C1   // warm neutral border
--text:        #2B2018   // warm near-black (not #000)
--text-muted:  #6E5D4E
```

Dark theme (this is where autumn shines — like dusk):

```
--accent-500:  #E07B39   // pumpkin, brighter for dark bg
--gold:        #E9B44C
--page-bg:     #1A1512   // deep warm charcoal-brown (not pure black)
--surface:     #241C16
--surface-alt: #2E241C
--border:      #3D2F24
--text:        #F0E6D8   // warm off-white
--text-muted:  #A89684
```

The important rule from `03-design-tokens.md`: **status/verdict/rating colors are a protected layer** and do not get "autumnified." AC stays green, WA stays red, etc. Because your surfaces are warm-neutral (not saturated), the green/red verdicts still read cleanly against them. The only tweak: nudge the "info" blue slightly toward teal so it doesn't clash with all the warm tones.

This slots straight into the token architecture — you'd add a "Warm Harvest" palette to the primitive tokens and keep the semantic layer intact.

## Custom artwork to commission/create

Prioritized by impact-per-effort:

**High value (do these first)**
1. **Hero / homepage banner** — a wide autumn scene (faling maple/ginkgo leaves, warm gradient sky) as a subtle backdrop behind the homepage header. Deliver at 2× for retina, and a dark-mode variant (dusk tones). Keep it low-contrast so text stays readable on top.
2. **Logo / wordmark treatment** — a small seasonal mark, e.g. the SQRT symbol (√) with a single faling leaf or a leaf integrated into the glyph. Provide light and dark versions as SVG.
3. **Seamless leaf-texture tile** — you already use tiled backgrounds (`base.scss` sets `background-repeat: repeat`). A very subtle, low-opacity autumn texture (paper grain + faint scattered leaves) replaces the current tiled images cleanly. Must be subtle enough not to fight tables.

**Medium value (personality)**
4. **Empty-state illustrations** — "no submissions yet," "no problems found," 404/500 pages. A raccoon/squirrel-with-acorn or a bare tree in autumn — small, friendly spot illustrations. Your `502.html` and `error.html` are natural homes.
5. **Rank/badge iconography** — reskin rank tiers with autumn-themed motifs (acorn → chestnut → maple leaf → golden leaf) while keeping the *rating colors* unchanged for recognizability.
6. **Decorative section dividers** — a thin leafy vine or branch as an `<hr>` replacement or section separator (SVG, tiny).

**Nice-to-have (seasonal delight)**
7. **Animated falling leaves** — a lightweight, `prefers-reduced-motion`-respecting CSS/JS effect on the homepage only. Must be off during contests and for reduced-motion users (see `07-accessibility.md`).
8. **Favicon / touch icons** — autumn-tinted version of your mark (you already ship a full favicon set referenced in `base.html`).
9. **OG/social share image** — autumn-branded default `og:image` (currently `/logo.png`).

## Format guidance for the artist

- **SVG** for logo, icons, dividers, empty states (scales, themeable, tiny).

# 08 — Autumn Theme ("Warm Harvest")

The **Warm Harvest** autumn theme is a concrete palette + artwork layer that sits
on top of the token architecture in `03-design-tokens.md`. It does not change the
token taxonomy or component specs; it only supplies a warm, seasonal set of
**primitive** values and remaps the **semantic** aliases to them.

The guiding rule: autumn owns the **brand and surface layers** (navbar, buttons,
links, backgrounds, borders, text). It never touches the **protected status
layer** — verdict colors (AC/WA/TLE…) and rating tiers keep their meanings so the
judge stays readable and color-vision-safe.

## 1. Palette identity

Warm Harvest is built around amber gold, pumpkin, and burnt sienna over
warm-neutral (paper) surfaces. Surfaces stay near-white in light mode and deep
warm-charcoal in dark mode so dense tables remain legible; the warmth comes from
accents, borders, and subtle tints, not from saturating the whole page.

| Role                | Light         | Dark          |
| ------------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| Primary brand       | Burnt sienna  | Pumpkin       |
| Secondary accent    | Amber gold    | Amber gold    |
| Page canvas         | Warm paper    | Warm charcoal |
| Text                | Warm near-black | Warm off-white |

## 2. Primitive palette (Warm Harvest)

These replace the neutral/green/blue primitives from `03-design-tokens.md §2.1`
when the autumn theme is active. Neutrals are intentionally *warm* (hue nudged
toward orange/brown) rather than cool gray.

### 2.1 Warm neutrals (0–1000)

| Primitive        | Value     | Notes                       |
| ---------------- | --------- | --------------------------- |
| `--neutral-0`    | `#ffffff` | pure white (cards, light)   |
| `--neutral-50`   | `#fbf6ef` | warm paper canvas (light)   |
| `--neutral-100`  | `#f4ebdd` | subtle warm surface (light) |
| `--neutral-200`  | `#e4d5c1` | borders (light)             |
| `--neutral-300`  | `#d3bfa4` |                             |
| `--neutral-400`  | `#a8907a` | muted text (light)          |
| `--neutral-500`  | `#8a7360` |                             |
| `--neutral-600`  | `#6e5d4e` | secondary text (light)      |
| `--neutral-700`  | `#4a3b2f` |                             |
| `--neutral-800`  | `#2e241c` | surface (dark)              |
| `--neutral-900`  | `#1a1512` | canvas (dark)               |
| `--neutral-1000` | `#120e0b` | deepest (dark)              |

### 2.2 Sienna (primary accent scale)

| Primitive       | Value     | Notes                        |
| --------------- | --------- | ---------------------------- |
| `--sienna-50`   | `#fbe9df` |                              |
| `--sienna-100`  | `#f6cdb6` |                              |
| `--sienna-300`  | `#e07b39` | pumpkin (bright accent)      |
| `--sienna-500`  | `#c1440e` | burnt sienna (brand)         |
| `--sienna-600`  | `#9e3609` | hover/active                 |
| `--sienna-700`  | `#7a2906` | navbar (light)               |
| `--sienna-800`  | `#551c04` |                              |

### 2.3 Gold (secondary accent scale)

| ------------- | --------- | ------------------------------ |
| `--gold-100`  | `#f7e6bd` |                                |
| `--gold-300`  | `#e9c46a` |                                |
| `--gold-500`  | `#e0a82e` | amber gold (the autumn yellow) |
| `--gold-600`  | `#c08d1e` |                                |

### 2.4 Info hue (teal-shifted)

The generic link/focus/info blue is shifted toward teal so it reads as
intentional against all the warm tones instead of clashing.

| Primitive     | Value     |
| ------------- | --------- |
| `--teal-300`  | `#5fb3c4` |
| `--teal-500`  | `#2c7a8c` |
| `--teal-600`  | `#1f5c6b` |

## 3. Semantic remapping

Same semantic tokens as `03-design-tokens.md §2.2`; only the primitive each one
points at changes for the autumn theme.

| Semantic token            | Role                     | Light → primitive | Dark → primitive |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| `--color-canvas`          | page background          | `--neutral-50`    | `--neutral-900`  |
| `--color-surface`         | cards, panels            | `--neutral-0`     | `--neutral-800`  |
| `--color-surface-raised`  | popovers, dropdowns      | `--neutral-0`     | `--neutral-700`  |
| `--color-surface-alt`     | zebra rows, subtle panel | `--neutral-100`   | `--neutral-700`  |
| `--color-border`          | default borders          | `--neutral-200`   | `--neutral-700`  |
| `--color-border-strong`   | emphasized borders       | `--neutral-300`   | `--neutral-600`  |
| `--color-text`            | primary text             | `--neutral-800`   | `--neutral-100`  |
| `--color-text-secondary`  | secondary text           | `--neutral-600`   | `--neutral-400`  |
| `--color-text-muted`      | hints, metadata          | `--neutral-400`   | `--neutral-500`  |
| `--color-text-inverse`    | text on accent bars      | `--neutral-0`     | `--neutral-0`    |
| `--color-accent`          | brand/action             | `--sienna-500`    | `--sienna-300`   |
| `--color-accent-hover`    | brand hover              | `--sienna-600`    | `--sienna-100`   |
| `--color-accent-contrast` | text/icon on accent      | `--neutral-0`     | `--neutral-1000` |
| `--color-accent-2`        | secondary accent (gold)  | `--gold-500`      | `--gold-300`     |
| `--color-navbar`          | top navigation bar       | `--sienna-700`    | `--neutral-1000` |
| `--color-link`            | link default             | `--teal-600`      | `--teal-300`     |
| `--color-link-hover`      | link hover               | `--sienna-500`    | `--gold-300`     |
| `--color-focus-ring`      | focus outline            | `--teal-500`      | `--teal-300`     |

Notes:
- `--color-accent-2` (gold) is a new semantic alias for the secondary accent used
  by badges, highlights, and hover glows. Add it to `03-design-tokens.md §2.2` when
  implemented.
- Link default is teal (not warm) so links stay distinguishable from the sienna
  brand actions; link **hover** warms toward sienna/gold for cohesion.

## 4. Protected layers (unchanged)

These are **not** recolored by the autumn theme. They keep the values in
`03-design-tokens.md`:

- **Verdict tokens** (`--verdict-ac`, `--verdict-wa`, …): AC stays green, WA stays
  red, TLE/MLE stay amber/blue. Warm-neutral surfaces keep them legible.
- **Rating tokens** (`--rating-newbie` … `--rating-grandmaster`): unchanged for
  cross-site recognizability.
- **Status semantics** (`--color-success-*`, `--color-danger-*`, etc.): success
  stays green, danger stays red. Only `--color-info-*` shifts to the teal family to
  fit the palette.

If a warm accent ever collides with a status color in context (e.g. gold badge next
to a warning), the status color wins and the accent is swapped for a neutral.

## 5. Artwork asset manifest

All decorative art is optional enhancement: pages MUST remain fully usable if an
asset fails to load. Store assets under `resources/autumn/`. Decorative art placed
behind text MUST be low-contrast/desaturated so it never threatens the WCAG AA
requirements in `07-accessibility.md`.

| ID   | Asset                     | Format         | Sizes / variants                 | Where used                          | Priority |
| ---- | ------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------- |
| A-1  | Homepage hero banner      | WebP + PNG     | 2× retina; light + dark variants | `templates/home.html` header        | High     |
| A-2  | Logo / wordmark (seasonal)| SVG            | light + dark                     | `templates/site-logo-fragment.html` | High     |
| A-3  | Seamless leaf/paper tile  | WebP           | tileable; light + dark           | `resources/base.scss` body bg       | High     |
| A-4  | Empty-state illustrations | SVG            | one per state                    | list empty states, `error.html`     | Medium   |
| A-5  | Error page art (404/500)  | SVG or PNG     | light + dark                     | `error.html`, `502.html`            | Medium   |
| A-6  | Rank/badge icons          | SVG            | one per rank tier                | `resources/ranks.scss` consumers    | Medium   |
| A-7  | Section divider (vine)    | SVG            | horizontal                       | `<hr>` / section separators         | Low      |
| A-8  | Falling-leaves effect     | CSS/JS + SVG   | reduced-motion aware; homepage   | `templates/home.html`               | Low      |
| A-9  | Favicon / touch icons     | ICO + PNG set  | full favicon set (see base.html) | site-wide `<head>`                  | Low      |
| A-10 | OG / social share image   | PNG            | 1200×630                         | default `og:image` in `base.html`   | Low      |

### Artwork guidelines

- **Vector first.** Logo, icons, dividers, and empty states as SVG — small,
  crisp, and themeable via `currentColor` where practical.
- **Raster where needed.** Hero and textures as WebP with a PNG fallback, at 2×.
- **Two variants.** Any art with baked-in colors needs a light and a dark version;
  reference them the way `base.scss` already branches on `$is_light_theme`.
- **Keep it behind, not on top.** Backgrounds sit under content at low opacity;
  never reduce text contrast below AA.
- **Palette-locked.** Use the Warm Harvest primitives above so art matches the UI.

### A-8 falling leaves — constraints

- Homepage only; never on contest, submission, or problem-solving pages.
- MUST be disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- MUST be lightweight (CSS transforms / a small canvas) and pause when the tab is
  hidden; it is decorative and MUST NOT block interaction or input.

## 6. Implementation notes

- This theme is a **palette swap**, so it plugs into Phase 0/1 of
  `06-implementation-roadmap.md`: define the Warm Harvest primitives, point the
  semantic aliases at them, and both light and dark modes follow automatically.
- Because theming is driven by `Profile.site_theme` + `DMOJ_THEME_CSS`
  (`04-technical-design.md`), Warm Harvest can ship as the default palette for both
  the light and dark stylesheets without new plumbing.
- The `--color-accent-2` (gold) and `--color-surface-alt` aliases are the only new
  tokens introduced here; fold them into `03-design-tokens.md` when implemented.
- Verify every remapped semantic pair against `07-accessibility.md` before shipping;
  warm low-contrast neutrals are the highest-risk area for AA text contrast.

# SQRTOJ Modern Competitive-Programming Design System

This directory contains the specification, requirements, technical design, and
task breakdown for the **Modern Competitive-Programming (MCP)** UI overhaul of
SQRTOJ.

The goal is a clean, content-dense, token-driven flat design that keeps the
information density a judge needs (scoreboards, submission tables, verdicts,
problem lists) while modernizing the look, unifying the color system, and making
dark mode a first-class, instantly switchable feature.

## Reading order

| # | Document | What it covers |
|---|----------|----------------|
| 1 | [`01-vision-and-principles.md`](01-vision-and-principles.md) | The design philosophy, target users, and the principles every decision is measured against. |
| 2 | [`02-requirements.md`](02-requirements.md) | Functional and non-functional requirements, scope, and acceptance criteria. |
| 3 | [`03-design-tokens.md`](03-design-tokens.md) | The token layer: color scales, typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion. The single source of visual truth. |
| 4 | [`04-technical-design.md`](04-technical-design.md) | How the system is implemented in the existing SCSS + `django_jinja` + `django_compressor` pipeline, theming architecture, and migration strategy. |
| 5 | [`05-component-specs.md`](05-component-specs.md) | Per-component visual and behavioral specs (navbar, buttons, tables, badges, forms, etc.). |
| 6 | [`06-implementation-roadmap.md`](06-implementation-roadmap.md) | Phased, checkbox task list with dependencies and estimates. |
| 7 | [`07-accessibility.md`](07-accessibility.md) | Contrast, focus, motion, and semantics requirements plus a verification checklist. |
| 8 | [`08-autumn-theme.md`](08-autumn-theme.md) | The "Warm Harvest" autumn palette (light + dark) mapped onto the token layer, plus the custom artwork asset manifest. |

## Current state (baseline)

Grounded in the repository as of this writing:

- **Styles** live in `resources/*.scss`, aggregated by `resources/style.scss`, and
  built into `style.css` (light) and `dark/style.css` (dark) by `make_style.sh`.
- **Theme values** are duplicated across `resources/vars-default.scss` (light) and
  `resources/vars-dark.scss` (dark), with shared tokens in
  `resources/vars-common.scss`. Both `@forward "vars-common"`.
- **Theme selection** is driven by `Profile.site_theme` (`auto` / `light` / `dark`,
  see `judge/models/choices.py`), surfaced to templates by
  `judge.template_context.site_theme`, and mapped to files via
  `DMOJ_THEME_CSS` in `dmoj/settings.py`. `templates/base.html` links the light
  and/or dark stylesheet, currently gated behind the `judge.test_site` permission.
- **Brand color** is a hardcoded green (`#045c20`) in `resources/navbar.scss`; the
  navigation bar background is set inline in `templates/base.html` (`#231F20`).
- **Link palette** is a separate blue scale, unrelated to the green brand color.
- **Typography** relies on system fonts (`Segoe UI`, `Lucida Grande`, `Arial`) with
  `Source Sans Pro` for the navbar; monospace uses a long fallback stack in
  `resources/vars-common.scss`.
- **Blog** already has a modern, well-considered token set (`$color_blog_*` in the
  `vars-*.scss` files) that is siloed to that feature. The MCP system generalizes
  that direction to the whole site.

## Non-goals

- No markup rewrite of every template in one pass. The rollout is incremental and
  ships value at each phase.
- No new frontend framework (no React/Vue/build-tool swap). We stay on
  server-rendered templates + SCSS + `django_compressor`.
- No change to the judging, contest, or submission *logic*. This is presentation
  only.
- No visual trend that harms readability (glassmorphism, neumorphism) — see
  `01-vision-and-principles.md`.

## How to contribute to this effort

Follow the conventions in the repository root `AGENTS.md`: match existing
DMOJ/VNOJ patterns, keep changes minimal and focused, run `flake8` for Python and
`npm run format:check` for websocket JS, and build styles with `./make_style.sh`
before finishing frontend work.

```

## User

btw, is the flat modern competitive programming design system also shipped

## Assistant

Good question, and it's worth being precise because it changes what I build.

## Short answer

The "Modern Competitive-Programming flat design" and "Warm Harvest" aren't two separate things. The MCP system is the **structure** (token layer, flat surfaces, spacing/radius/elevation scale, typography, component treatment). Warm Harvest is just **which color values fill the token slots**. So shipping Warm Harvest as the default *is* shipping the flat MCP system — with autumn colors instead of the old green/blue.

## But "ship all of it in one go" is the wrong move

Your own roadmap (`06`) splits this into Phases 0–4 for a reason. Rewriting all ~20 SCSS partials and dozens of templates in a single PR is high-risk, hard to review, and easy to regress. The realistic, correct scope for *this* PR is the **foundation that makes it a real design system**, which is:

1. **Token layer** — emit `:root` CSS custom properties (colors, spacing, radius, elevation, type, motion) as the single source of truth.
2. **Theming architecture** — wire the two built stylesheets to the tokens so light/dark both follow automatically.
3. **Summer backup** — preserve today's green/blue palette as a selectable "Summer" theme.
4. **Warm Harvest default** — the autumn palette fills the tokens; ships as the default for both light and dark.
5. **Flat treatment on core primitives** — aply the flat look (surfaces, borders, radius, elevation, focus rings) to the highest-traffic shared pieces: navbar, buttons, tables, badges, links. These cascade site-wide.

The page-by-page long tail (problem statement layout, scoreboard composition, etc.) stays as follow-up phases — that's deliberate, not incomplete. Trying to cram it all in would violate the "kep changes minimal and focused / incremental and shippable" principle the docs are built on.

## What "test all" will actually mean here

I checked the tolchain: Node 26, sass 1.101, npm 11, Python 3.14 are present. So I can run the **style build** (`./make_style.sh`) for real to prove both themes compile. The Django suite (`python manage.py test judge`) needs MySQL + the full requirements installed, which likely isn't set up in this environment — I'll attempt it and report honestly if it can't run, rather than claiming a pass. Since this PR is CSS/SCSS + template + one settings change, the style build + `flake8` on any touched Python is the meaningful gate anyway.

So, to confirm before I start writing code: I'll ship **the foundation + core-primitive flat styling with Warm Harvest as default and Summer as the backup theme**, close the spec gaps, build both stylesheets to verify, and leave the per-page polish as documented follow-up phases. 

Want me to proceed on that basis? If you'd rather I also grind through every page's layout in this same PR, say so and I'll expand the scope — but I'd recommend against it.

````SQRTOJ/docs/design-system/04-technical-design.md
     1	# 04 — Technical Design
     2	
     3	How the design system is implemented on top of the existing Django + SCSS +
     4	`django-compressor` pipeline, with minimal risk and full backward compatibility.
     5	
     6	## 1. Current architecture (as-is)
     7	
     8	Grounded in the repository:
     9	
    10	- **Build**: `make_style.sh` copies `resources/vars-<theme>.scss` → `resources/vars.scss`,
    11	  runs `sass resources:sass_processed`, then `postcss` with `autoprefixer`, writing
    12	  `resources/style.css` (light) and `resources/dark/style.css` (dark).
    13	- **Entry point**: `resources/style.scss` `@import`s `base`, `navbar`, `table`,
    14	  `problem`, `status`, `submission`, `contest`, etc. Each imports `vars` (which is
    15	  the copied theme file), so the two themes are two full compiled stylesheets.
    16	- **Tokens today**: SCSS variables split across `vars-common.scss` (shared:
    17	  `$base_font_size`, `$widget_border_radius`, `$monospace-fonts`),
    18	  `vars-default.scss` (light), and `vars-dark.scss` (dark). Blog already added a
    19	  richer `$color_blog_*` set.
    20	- **Theme selection**: `Profile.site_theme` (`auto`/`light`/`dark`, see
    21	  `judge/models/choices.py` `SITE_THEMES`). `judge/template_context.py::site_theme`
    22	  exposes `LIGHT_STYLE_CSS`, `DARK_STYLE_CSS`, `PREFERRED_STYLE_CSS` from
    23	  `settings.DMOJ_THEME_CSS = {'light': 'style.css', 'dark': 'dark/style.css'}`.
    24	- **Template**: `templates/base.html` links either a single `PREFERRED_STYLE_CSS`
    25	  or both light/dark via `media="(prefers-color-scheme: ...)"`, but only for users
    26	  with the `judge.test_site` permission; everyone else gets `LIGHT_STYLE_CSS`. A
    27	  `TODO` notes dark mode should ship for all users once it's solid.
    28	
    29	### Constraints this imposes
    30	
    31	- Every visual value is baked into two compiled CSS files. Theme switching means
    32	  loading a different file; there is no runtime variable layer.
    33	- `django-compressor` (`{% compress css %}`) concatenates/minifies at deploy; the
    34	  linked hrefs come from `static(...)`.
    35	- We must not break the `make_style.sh` outputs or the `DMOJ_THEME_CSS` contract.
    36	
    37	## 2. Target architecture (to-be)
    38	
    39	Introduce a **CSS custom-property token layer** that both compiled themes emit,
    40	while keeping SCSS for structure. This is additive and backward compatible.
    41	
    42	```mermaid
    43	graph TD
    44	    P[vars-primitives.scss<br/>raw palette + scales] --> D[vars-default.scss]
    45	    P --> K[vars-dark.scss]
    46	    D --> E[emit-tokens.scss<br/>:root maps to semantic CSS vars]
    47	    K --> E
    48	    E --> S[style.scss entry]
    49	    S --> C[Component partials<br/>consume var --color-*, --space-*, ...]
    50	    C --> B[make_style.sh]
    51	    B --> L[style.css light]
    52	    B --> R[dark/style.css dark]
    53	```
    54	
    55	### 2.1 Token emission strategy
    56	
    57	Two viable approaches; **Approach A is recommended**.
    58	
    59	**Approach A — Semantic vars emitted per compiled theme (recommended).**
    60	Each theme file still exists, but instead of components reading SCSS `$color_*`
    61	directly, a shared partial emits a `:root { ... }` block mapping semantic CSS
    62	variables to that theme's values.
    63	
    64	- `style.css` (light build) emits light values into `:root`.
    65	- `dark/style.css` (dark build) emits dark values into `:root`.
    66	- Components reference `var(--color-surface)` etc., never the SCSS var.
    67	
    68	Pros: zero change to `make_style.sh`, the `DMOJ_THEME_CSS` contract, or how
    69	`base.html` links files. Instant groundwork for a future single-file runtime
    70	toggle. Lowest risk.
    71	
    72	Cons: still ships two files (fine — matches today).
    73	
    74	**Approach B — Single stylesheet with `[data-theme]` runtime switch.**
    75	Emit both light and dark token blocks in one CSS file:
    76	`:root { light } :root[data-theme="dark"] { dark }`, toggled by a `data-theme`
    77	attribute on `<html>` set from `Profile.site_theme` (and `prefers-color-scheme`
    78	for `auto`). One compiled stylesheet for structure + one for tokens.
    79	
    80	Pros: instant theme switching with no reload, no flash; enables user theme toggle;
    81	smaller conceptual model.
    82	
    83	Cons: larger change to `make_style.sh`, `base.html`, and `template_context`;
    84	requires an inline no-flash script. Defer to a later phase.
    85	
    86	**Decision:** implement Approach A first (Phase 1–2), keep the door open to migrate
    87	to Approach B in a later phase once tokens are proven. See `06-roadmap-and-tasks.md`.
    88	
    89	### 2.2 File layout changes
    90	
    91	New/refactored files under `resources/`:
    92	
    93	```
    94	resources/
    95	  vars-primitives.scss     # NEW: raw palettes + numeric scales (theme-independent)
    96	  vars-common.scss         # KEEP: non-color shared (fonts stack names, base size)
    97	  vars-default.scss        # REFACTOR: light semantic map (SCSS vars) + @forward primitives
    98	  vars-dark.scss           # REFACTOR: dark semantic map (SCSS vars) + @forward primitives
    99	  _emit-tokens.scss        # NEW: emits :root { --color-*: ...; --space-*: ...; }
   100	  _mixins.scss             # NEW: helpers (focus-ring, elevation, truncation, media)
   101	  style.scss               # UPDATE: @import "emit-tokens" before component partials
   102	  base.scss                # UPDATE: consume tokens (background, typography, links)
   103	  navbar.scss ...          # UPDATE incrementally per component roadmap
   104	```
   105	
   106	`_emit-tokens.scss` is a fragment (leading underscore) so `sass` won't compile it
   107	standalone. `style.scss` imports it once, right after `vars`, so `:root` is defined
   108	before any component rule uses `var(--...)`.
   109	
   110	### 2.3 Backward-compatible token bridging
   111	
   112	To avoid a big-bang rewrite, keep the legacy SCSS variables working during
   113	migration by defining them in terms of the new tokens (or vice versa). Concretely,
   114	in each theme file the semantic SCSS vars and the primitives coexist, and
   115	`_emit-tokens.scss` maps them to CSS vars. Legacy names like `$color_primary10`
   116	remain valid until their consumers are migrated, then are removed.
   117	
   118	Migration rule: when a component partial is touched, convert its hardcoded values
   119	and legacy `$color_*` refs to `var(--...)` tokens. Untouched partials keep
   120	compiling unchanged.
   121	
   122	## 3. Theming and no-flash behavior
   123	
   124	Phase 1–2 (Approach A) keeps the current mechanism: `base.html` links the correct
   125	compiled file based on `PREFERRED_STYLE_CSS` / `prefers-color-scheme`. No new flash
   126	risk because the browser picks the stylesheet before paint via the `media` query.
   127	
   128	When/if Approach B lands:
   129	
   130	- Set `<html data-theme="...">` server-side from `request.profile.site_theme` so
   131	  there is no flash for logged-in users.
   132	- For `auto`, inline a tiny blocking script in `<head>` that reads
   133	  `prefers-color-scheme` and sets `data-theme` before first paint.
   134	- Keep `DMOJ_THEME_CSS` working; the structural stylesheet stays a single link.
   135	
   136	## 4. Rollout gating (test_site permission)
   137	
   138	Reuse the existing `judge.test_site` permission and the `base.html` branch to ship
   139	the redesign to opt-in users first (matches the current dark-mode gating and
   140	`ProfileForm`'s "Enable experimental features" toggle). Concretely:
   141	
   142	- Build the redesigned stylesheet(s) and expose them via new
   143	  `DMOJ_THEME_CSS`-style settings (e.g. behind a setting flag), OR
   144	- Land token + component changes directly in the existing stylesheets but keep any
   145	  layout-breaking changes gated until validated.
   146	
   147	Prefer the incremental in-place approach (tokens are backward compatible), using
   148	`test_site` only for changes that visibly alter layout, so the general redesign can
   149	graduate by simply flipping the default — consistent with the `base.html` `TODO`.
   150	
   151	Any new setting follows the repo convention (`DMOJ_*` / `VNOJ_*` in
   152	`dmoj/settings.py`, documented, not hardcoded — see `AGENTS.md`).
   153	
   154	## 5. Build, lint, and verification impact
   155	
   156	- **Styles build**: `./make_style.sh` must succeed for both themes after each
   157	  change (needs `npm ci` for `postcss`/`sass`/`autoprefixer`). This is the primary
   158	  gate for CSS work (mirrors the `styles` CI job in `.github/workflows/build.yml`).
   159	- **Browser support**: CSS custom properties and the color values are covered by
   160	  the project's `.browserslistrc`/`autoprefixer`; verify no target in
   161	  `caniuse.json` regresses. Custom properties are broadly supported by the existing
   162	  targets; confirm during Phase 1.
   163	- **Python/tests**: no model or view changes are required for Phase 1–2, so
   164	  `python manage.py test judge` and `flake8` are unaffected. If a settings flag or
   165	  `template_context` change is added later, include it in the same change and keep
   166	  `flake8` clean (max line length 120, pycharm import order).
   167	- **Websocket**: unaffected; `npm run format:check` scope is `websocket/` only.
   168	
   169	## 6. Risks and mitigations
   170	
   171	| Risk                                             | Mitigation                                                        |
   172	| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
   173	| Big-bang refactor breaks many pages              | Token layer is additive; migrate partials one at a time (Phase 3).|
   174	| Dark mode regressions for existing users         | Keep `test_site` gating for layout-affecting changes.             |
   175	| `django-compressor` caching serves stale CSS     | Rely on existing compressor hashing; bump on deploy as today.     |
   176	| Web font loading hurts LCP                        | `font-display: swap`, system-font fallback, self-host if needed.  |
   177	| Color contrast regressions                        | Validate every semantic pair against `07-accessibility.md`.       |
   178	| Legacy `$color_*` refs left dangling after rename | Remove a primitive only when all consumers are migrated.          |
   179	
   180	## 7. Definition of done (technical)
   181	
   182	- `vars-primitives.scss` + `_emit-tokens.scss` exist; both compiled themes emit the
   183	  full semantic token set to `:root`.
   184	- `make_style.sh` builds both themes with no errors and no new `autoprefixer`
   185	  warnings for supported browsers.
   186	- At least the Phase-2 core components consume tokens only (no hardcoded hex in
   187	  those partials).
   188	- Documentation values (03) match the implemented token values.
   189	- No regression in `flake8`, `manage.py test judge`, or `npm run format:check`.

````

    13	## 1. Color & contrast
    14	
    15	- Body text vs. background: contrast ratio **≥ 4.5:1**.

// Design-system token layer (Phase 0).
//
// Emits the semantic design tokens from docs/design-system/03-design-tokens.md as
// CSS custom properties on :root. This partial is imported once by style.scss,
// after the theme `vars` file has defined `$is_light_theme`, so the light build
// (style.css) emits the light values and the dark build (dark/style.css) emits the
// dark values.
//
// Phase 0 is additive and backward compatible: these variables are DEFINED but not
// yet CONSUMED by component partials. The values below intentionally match the
// current green/blue palette so there is no visual change. Later phases migrate
// components to `var(--...)` and swap the palette (see 06-implementation-roadmap.md).

:root {
    // --- Color: surfaces & text ---
    @if $is_light_theme {
        --color-canvas: #f8f9fa;
        --color-surface: #ffffff;
        --color-surface-raised: #ffffff;
        --color-surface-alt: #eef0f2;
        --color-border: #dfe3e6;
        --color-border-strong: #c4cbd1;
        --color-text: #20262b;
        --color-text-secondary: #4b545c;
        --color-text-muted: #9aa4ad;
        --color-text-inverse: #ffffff;

        --color-accent: #1ba94c;
        --color-accent-hover: #158a3e;
        --color-accent-contrast: #ffffff;
        --color-accent-2: #5fc27e;
        --color-navbar: #045c20;

        --color-link: #1958c1;
        --color-link-hover: #0645ad;
        --color-focus-ring: #1958c1;

        --color-info-bg: #ddeeff;
        --color-info-fg: #26536b;
        --color-success-bg: #ddf3e4;
        --color-success-fg: #177a3a;
        --color-warning-bg: #fff3cd;
        --color-warning-fg: #8a6100;
        --color-danger-bg: #f8dcdc;
        --color-danger-fg: #a52222;
    } @else {
        --color-canvas: #161b1f;
        --color-surface: #20262b;
        --color-surface-raised: #333b42;
        --color-surface-alt: #333b42;
        --color-border: #333b42;
        --color-border-strong: #4b545c;
        --color-text: #eef0f2;
        --color-text-secondary: #9aa4ad;
        --color-text-muted: #6b757e;
        --color-text-inverse: #ffffff;

        --color-accent: #1ba94c;
        --color-accent-hover: #5fc27e;
        --color-accent-contrast: #ffffff;
        --color-accent-2: #5fc27e;
        --color-navbar: #0f1214;

        --color-link: #6bb0f5;
        --color-link-hover: #8fc4ff;
        --color-focus-ring: #6bb0f5;

        --color-info-bg: #002233;
        --color-info-fg: #77ddff;
        --color-success-bg: #0e3a22;
        --color-success-fg: #66ff88;
        --color-warning-bg: #3a2e05;
        --color-warning-fg: #ffdd66;
        --color-danger-bg: #3a1414;
        --color-danger-fg: #ff9999;
    }

    // --- Color: rating tiers ---
    @if $is_light_theme {
        --rating-none: #999999;
        --rating-newbie: #808080;
        --rating-pupil: #008000;
        --rating-specialist: #03a89e;
        --rating-expert: #0000ff;
        --rating-candidate-master: #aa00aa;
        --rating-master: #ff8c00;
        --rating-grandmaster: #ff0000;
    } @else {
        --rating-none: #aaaaaa;
        --rating-newbie: #988f81;
        --rating-pupil: #72ff72;
        --rating-specialist: #57fcf2;
        --rating-expert: #337dff;
        --rating-candidate-master: #ff55ff;
        --rating-master: #ff981a;
        --rating-grandmaster: #ff1a1a;
    }

    // --- Spacing (4px base) ---
    --space-0: 0;
    --space-1: 4px;
    --space-2: 8px;
    --space-3: 12px;
    --space-4: 16px;
    --space-5: 24px;
    --space-6: 32px;
    --space-7: 48px;
    --space-8: 64px;

    // --- Radius ---
    --radius-sm: 4px;
    --radius-md: 8px;
    --radius-lg: 12px;
    --radius-pill: 999px;

    // --- Elevation ---
    @if $is_light_theme {
        --shadow-0: none;
        --shadow-1: 0 1px 2px rgba(16, 24, 32, 0.08);
        --shadow-2: 0 2px 8px rgba(16, 24, 32, 0.1);
        --shadow-3: 0 8px 24px rgba(16, 24, 32, 0.14);
    } @else {
        --shadow-0: none;
        --shadow-1: 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
        --shadow-2: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55);
        --shadow-3: 0 8px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6);
    }

    // --- Typography ---
    --font-ui: "Inter", "Segoe UI", "Lucida Grande", Arial, sans-serif;
    --font-mono: "JetBrains Mono", "Fira Code", Consolas, "DejaVu Sans Mono", monospace;

    --text-xs: 12px;
    --text-sm: 13px;
    --text-base: 15px;
    --text-md: 17px;
    --text-lg: 20px;
    --text-xl: 24px;
    --text-2xl: 30px;

    --leading-xs: 1.4;
    --leading-sm: 1.45;
    --leading-base: 1.55;
    --leading-md: 1.5;
    --leading-lg: 1.4;
    --leading-xl: 1.3;
    --leading-2xl: 1.25;

    --weight-regular: 400;
    --weight-medium: 500;
    --weight-semibold: 600;
    --weight-bold: 700;

    // --- Motion ---
    --motion-fast: 120ms;
    --motion-base: 200ms;
    --motion-slow: 320ms;
    --ease-standard: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);

    // --- Z-index ---
    --z-base: 0;
    --z-dropdown: 1000;
    --z-navbar: 1000;
    --z-overlay: 1100;
    --z-modal: 1110;
    --z-toast: 1200;
}

```

   105	| `--color-link-hover`      | link hover               | `--sienna-500`    | `--gold-300`     |
   106	| `--color-focus-ring`      | focus outline            | `--teal-500`      | `--teal-300`     |
   107	
   108	Notes:

   112	- Link default is teal (not warm) so links stay distinguishable from the sienna

// Brand accent + navbar surface. Declared with !default so each palette file can
// override them (Warm Harvest -> sienna/pumpkin; Summer keeps the original green).
// Consumed by shared component partials (navbar, table, widgets) that only import
// vars-common, so the value must live here rather than in a palette-only file.
$highlight_blue: #1ba94c !default;
$color_navbar_bg: #045c20 !default;
$announcement_red: #ae0000 !default;

$base_font_size: 15px;
$widget_border_radius: 4px;

$table_header_rounding: 6px;

## Assistant

The navbar uses hardcoded `#045c20` in several places. It imports `vars-common`, which now has `$color_navbar_bg`. Let me replace those hardcoded grens with the variable so Summer stays green and Warm Harvest goes sienna.

**Tool Call: resources/navbar.scss**

Diff: resources/navbar.scss
```
// Navbar should look the same in every theme, so vars-common should be enough.
@import "vars-common";

#user-links {
    top: 0;
    right: 0;
    position: absolute;
    color: #fff;
    padding-right: 10px;
    display: inline-flex;
    min-height: 100%;
    align-items: center;
    white-space: nowrap;

    a {
        color: #FFF;
    }

    li {
        text-transform: none;
    }

    &>ul {
        display: block;
        margin: 0;

        &>li {
            &>a {
                display: block;
                padding: 0;
                height: 100%;

                &>span {
                    font-size: 13px;
                    padding: 10px 10px;
                    display: block;
                    white-space: nowrap;

                    &>img {
                        vertical-align: middle;
                        border-radius: $widget_border_radius;
                        margin-right: 6px;
                    }

                    &>span {
                        vertical-align: middle;
                        color: #eee;
                    }
                }
            }

            &>ul {
                left: 0;
            }
        }
    }
}

#nav-background {
    position: absolute;
    z-index: 3;
    top: 0;
    left: 0;
    width: 100%;
    height: 48px;
    background: $color_navbar_bg;
}

#nav-shadow {
    height: 3px;
    background: linear-gradient(rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5), transparent);
}

#nav-container {
    background: $color_navbar_bg;

    // opacity: 0.77
    // filter: alpha(opacity=77)
    height: 100%;
}

nav {
    position: fixed;
    top: 0;
    left: 0;
    right: 0;
    z-index: 500;

    ul {
        margin: 0 0 0 -5px;
        padding: 0 0 0 1%;
        display: block;

        li {
            display: inline-block;
            color: #FFF;
            text-transform: uppercase;
            position: relative;
            font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', sans-serif;

            &.home-nav-element a {
                padding: 0;
                height: 44px;

                &:hover {
                    border-bottom: none;
                    padding-top: 0;
                    padding-bottom: 0;
                }
            }

            a,
            button {
                text-decoration: none;
                vertical-align: middle;
                color: #FFF;
                padding: 14px 7px;
                height: 20px;
                display: inline-table;

                &:link {
                    color: #FFF;
                }

                &:hover {
                    color: #FFF;
                    background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25);
                    margin: 0;
                }

                &.active {
                    color: #FFF;

                    border: 5px solid transparent;
                    border-bottom: 5px solid $highlight_blue;
                    padding: 9px 2px;
                }

                .nav-expand {
                    display: none;
                }
            }

            ul {
                padding: 0;
                position: absolute;
                left: 5px;
                display: none;
                color: #fff;
                background: $color_navbar_bg;
                margin: 0 !important;
                box-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);

                li {
                    a.active {
                        border: none;
                        border-left: 5px solid $highlight_blue;
                    }
                }

                li {
                    display: block;

                    a,
                    button {
                        padding: 8px 20px 8px 8px !important;
                        font-size: 0.8em;
                        line-height: 18px;
                        display: block;
                        border-left: 4px solid $highlight_blue;
                        white-space: nowrap;
                    }
                }
            }

            button {
                background: none;
                text-align: left;
                border: none;
                width: 100%;
                border-radius: 0;
                height: auto;
            }

            &:hover>ul,
            &:active>ul,
            &:focus>ul {
                display: block !important;
            }

            &.home-nav-element a:hover {
                border-bottom: 0;
                padding-top: 0;
                padding-bottom: 0;
                background: transparent;
            }
        }
    }

    .nav-divider {
        width: 1px;
        vertical-align: middle;
        padding-left: 3px;
        display: inline-block;
        height: 32px;
        margin-right: 1px;
        border-right: 3px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15);
    }
}

#navicon {
    display: none;
}

@media (max-width: 760px) {
    #navigation {
        height: 36px;
    }

    #navicon {
        transition-duration: 0.25s;
        display: block;
        line-height: 26px;
        font-size: 2em;
        color: #FFF;
        padding: 0 0.25em;
        margin: 4px 0.25em;
        white-space: nowrap;
        float: left;

        &.hover {
            color: #4db7fe;
            text-shadow: 0 0 5px $highlight_blue;
            transition-duration: 0.25s;
        }
    }

    #nav-list {
        display: none;
        padding: 0;
        margin: 0;
        position: fixed;
        top: 36px;
        background: $color_navbar_bg;
        bottom: 0;
        width: 8em;
        left: 0;

        &.show-list {
            display: block;
        }

        li {
            display: block;

            a {
                display: block;

                .nav-expand {
                    float: right;
                    display: block;
                    height: inherit;
                    margin: (-13px) -7px;
                    padding: inherit;
                }
            }

            ul {
                left: 8em;
                top: 0px;

                &.show-list {
                    display: block;
                }
            }

            &.home-nav-element {
                display: none;
            }
        }
    }

    #user-links>ul>li>a>span {
        padding: 6px 8px;
    }
}

@media not all and (max-width: 760px) {
    #nav-list {
        li {
            &.home-menu-item {
                display: none;
            }

            &:not(:hover)>ul {
                display: none !important;
            }

            ul {
                left: 0 !important;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

// Navbar brand color is theme-coupled (sienna for Warm Harvest, green for Summer),
// so import the full theme `vars` to pick up $color_navbar_bg / $highlight_blue.
@import "vars";

#user-links {
    top: 0;
    right: 0;
    position: absolute;
    color: #fff;
    padding-right: 10px;
    display: inline-flex;
    min-height: 100%;
    align-items: center;
    white-space: nowrap;

    a {
        color: #FFF;
    }

    li {
        text-transform: none;
    }

    &>ul {
        display: block;
        margin: 0;

        &>li {
            &>a {
                display: block;
                padding: 0;
                height: 100%;

                &>span {
                    font-size: 13px;
                    padding: 10px 10px;
                    display: block;
                    white-space: nowrap;

                    &>img {
                        vertical-align: middle;
                        border-radius: $widget_border_radius;
                        margin-right: 6px;
                    }

                    &>span {
                        vertical-align: middle;
                        color: #eee;
                    }
                }
            }

            &>ul {
                left: 0;
            }
        }
    }
}

#nav-background {
    position: absolute;
    z-index: 3;
    top: 0;
    left: 0;
    width: 100%;
    height: 48px;
    background: $color_navbar_bg;
}

#nav-shadow {
    height: 3px;
    background: linear-gradient(rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5), transparent);
}

#nav-container {
    background: $color_navbar_bg;

    // opacity: 0.77
    // filter: alpha(opacity=77)
    height: 100%;
}

nav {
    position: fixed;
    top: 0;
    left: 0;
    right: 0;
    z-index: 500;

    ul {
        margin: 0 0 0 -5px;
        padding: 0 0 0 1%;
        display: block;

        li {
            display: inline-block;
            color: #FFF;
            text-transform: uppercase;
            position: relative;
            font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', sans-serif;

            &.home-nav-element a {
                padding: 0;
                height: 44px;

                &:hover {
                    border-bottom: none;
                    padding-top: 0;
                    padding-bottom: 0;
                }
            }

            a,
            button {
                text-decoration: none;
                vertical-align: middle;
                color: #FFF;
                padding: 14px 7px;
                height: 20px;
                display: inline-table;

                &:link {
                    color: #FFF;
                }

                &:hover {
                    color: #FFF;
                    background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25);
                    margin: 0;
                }

                &.active {
                    color: #FFF;

                    border: 5px solid transparent;
                    border-bottom: 5px solid $highlight_blue;
                    padding: 9px 2px;
                }

                .nav-expand {
                    display: none;
                }
            }

            ul {
                padding: 0;
                position: absolute;
                left: 5px;
                display: none;
                color: #fff;
                background: $color_navbar_bg;
                margin: 0 !important;
                box-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);

                li {
                    a.active {
                        border: none;
                        border-left: 5px solid $highlight_blue;
                    }
                }

                li {
                    display: block;

                    a,
                    button {
                        padding: 8px 20px 8px 8px !important;
                        font-size: 0.8em;
                        line-height: 18px;
                        display: block;
                        border-left: 4px solid $highlight_blue;
                        white-space: nowrap;
                    }
                }
            }

            button {
                background: none;
                text-align: left;
                border: none;
                width: 100%;
                border-radius: 0;
                height: auto;
            }

            &:hover>ul,
            &:active>ul,
            &:focus>ul {
                display: block !important;
            }

            &.home-nav-element a:hover {
                border-bottom: 0;
                padding-top: 0;
                padding-bottom: 0;
                background: transparent;
            }
        }
    }

    .nav-divider {
        width: 1px;
        vertical-align: middle;
        padding-left: 3px;
        display: inline-block;
        height: 32px;
        margin-right: 1px;
        border-right: 3px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15);
    }
}

#navicon {
    display: none;
}

@media (max-width: 760px) {
    #navigation {
        height: 36px;
    }

    #navicon {
        transition-duration: 0.25s;
        display: block;
        line-height: 26px;
        font-size: 2em;
        color: #FFF;
        padding: 0 0.25em;
        margin: 4px 0.25em;
        white-space: nowrap;
        float: left;

        &.hover {
            color: #4db7fe;
            text-shadow: 0 0 5px $highlight_blue;
            transition-duration: 0.25s;
        }
    }

    #nav-list {
        display: none;
        padding: 0;
        margin: 0;
        position: fixed;
        top: 36px;
        background: $color_navbar_bg;
        bottom: 0;
        width: 8em;
        left: 0;

        &.show-list {
            display: block;
        }

        li {
            display: block;

            a {
                display: block;

                .nav-expand {
                    float: right;
                    display: block;
                    height: inherit;
                    margin: (-13px) -7px;
                    padding: inherit;
                }
            }

            ul {
                left: 8em;
                top: 0px;

                &.show-list {
                    display: block;
                }
            }

            &.home-nav-element {
                display: none;
            }
        }
    }

    #user-links>ul>li>a>span {
        padding: 6px 8px;
    }
}

@media not all and (max-width: 760px) {
    #nav-list {
        li {
            &.home-menu-item {
                display: none;
            }

            &:not(:hover)>ul {
                display: none !important;
            }

            ul {
                left: 0 !important;
            }
        }
    }
}

@import "vars";

$is_light_theme: true;

.h-scrollable-table {
    overflow-x: auto;
}

.table {
    border-spacing: 0;
    width: 100%;
    margin-left: auto;
    margin-right: auto;
    margin-bottom: 0.5em;
    background: rgba($color_primary100, 0.01);
    backdrop-filter: blur(3px);

    &.striped tr:nth-child(2n) {
        background: rgba($color_primary100, 0.03);
    }

    th {
        height: 2em;
        @if $is_light_theme {
            color: #fff;
        }
        @else {
            color: #ccc;
        }
        background-color: $color_navbar_bg;
        border-color: $color_primary50;
        border-width: 0 1px 1px 0;
        border-style: solid;
        padding: 4px 10px;
        vertical-align: middle;
        text-align: center;
        white-space: nowrap;
        font-weight: 600;
        font-size: 1.1em;
        border-radius: 0;
    }

    td {
        border-color: $color_primary25;
        border-width: 0 1px 1px 0;
        border-style: solid;
        padding: 7px 5px;
        vertical-align: middle;
        text-align: center;
        border-radius: 0;
    }

    // Border fixes
    th:first-child, td:first-child {
        border-left-width: 1px;
    }

    tr:first-child th, tr:first-child td {
        border-top-width: 1px;
    }

    th:last-child, td:last-child {
        border-right-width: 1px;
    }

}

@import "vars";

$is_light_theme: true;

.social i {
    display: inline;
    font-size: 1.9em;
}

.facebook-this, .tweet-this {
    display: inline;
}

.tweet-this i {
    color: #55ACEE;
}

.facebook-this i {
    color: #133783;
}

.social {
    font-size: 1.3em;
    float: right;
}

// Bootstrap-y buttons
.button, button, input[type=submit] {
    color: white !important;
    text-decoration: none !important;
    cursor: pointer;
    vertical-align: middle;
    white-space: nowrap;
    font-weight: 400;
    line-height: 1.4;
    background: rgb(51, 122, 183) none repeat scroll 0 (0% / auto) padding-box border-box;
    background: -webkit-linear-gradient(top, #337ab7 0, #265a88 100%) repeat-x;
    background: linear-gradient(to bottom, #337ab7 0, #265a88 100%) repeat-x;
    border-radius: $widget_border_radius;
    padding: 6px 12px;
    display: block;
    border: 0;
    text-align: center;

    // 4k hack
    font-size: $base_font_size;

    &:hover {
        background: #265a88;
    }

    &:active {
        border-color: #245580;
        background: #265a88;
    }

    &.full {
        padding: 6px 0;
    }

    &.disabled {
        background: linear-gradient(to bottom, darkgray 0, gray 100%) repeat-x !important;
        border-color: grey !important;
        cursor: not-allowed;
    }
}

.inline-button {
    display: inline;
    vertical-align: top;
    padding: 3px 6px;
}

input {
    &[type=text], &[type=password], &[type=email], &[type=number], &[type=url] {
        padding: 4px 8px;
        color: $color_primary75;
        background: $color_primary0 none;
        border: 1px solid $color_primary25;
        border-radius: $widget_border_radius;
        box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba($color_primary100, 0.075) inset;
        transition: border-color 0.15s ease-in-out 0s, box-shadow 0.15s ease-in-out 0s;
        box-sizing: border-box;

        // Need this explicitly because UA stylesheet for Chrome on 4k makes
        // everything look bad otherwise (forces it to 9.3px)
        font-size: $base_font_size;

        &:hover {
            border-color: rgba(82, 168, 236, 0.8);
            box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba($color_primary100, 0.075), 0 0 4px rgba(82, 168, 236, 0.6);
        }

        &:focus {
            border-color: rgba(82, 168, 236, 0.8);
            box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba($color_primary100, 0.075), 0 0 8px rgba(82, 168, 236, 0.6);
            outline: 0;
        }
    }

    &[type=number] {
        padding: 2px 0 2px 5px;
    }

    &[type=checkbox] {
        appearance: none;
        vertical-align: middle;
        border: 1px solid $color_primary50;
        background: $color_primary0;
        border-radius: 2px;
        width: 0.95em;
        height: 0.95em;
        cursor: pointer;

        &:checked {
            appearance: auto;
            accent-color: $highlight_blue;
        }
    }
}

textarea {
    padding: 4px 8px;
    color: $color_primary75;
    background: $color_primary0 none;
    border: 1px solid $color_primary25;
    border-radius: $widget_border_radius;
    box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba($color_primary100, 0.075) inset;
    transition: border-color 0.15s ease-in-out 0s, box-shadow 0.15s ease-in-out 0s;
    box-sizing: border-box;
}

textarea:hover {
    border-color: rgba(82, 168, 236, 0.8);
    box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba($color_primary100, 0.075), 0 0 4px rgba(82, 168, 236, 0.6);
}

textarea:focus {
    border-color: rgba(82, 168, 236, 0.8);
    box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba($color_primary100, 0.075), 0 0 8px rgba(82, 168, 236, 0.6);
    outline: 0;
}

// Bootstrap-y copy button
.btn-clipboard {
    top: 0;
    right: 0;
    display: block;
    font-size: 12px;
    font-weight: bold;
    color: $color_primary50;
    cursor: pointer;
    background-color: $color_pageBg;
    border: 1px solid $color_primary25;
    border-radius: 0 $widget_border_radius;
    position: absolute;
    padding: 5px 8px;
}

    position: relative;
    margin-top: 1.5em;
}

// Bootstrap-y tabs
.ul_tab_a_active {
    color: $color_primary100;
    // Cover up the bottom border of active tabs with this color
    background: $color_pageBg;
    cursor: default;
    border: 1px solid $color_primary25;

}

.tabs {

    > ul {

        > li {

ul.pagination a:hover {

            }

            > {
                a, span {

                    float: left;
                    padding: 4px 12px;
                    line-height: 1.42857;
                    text-decoration: none;
                    color: $color_primary0;
                    background-color: $color_primary75;
                    border: 1px solid $color_primary50;
                    margin-left: -1px;
                }
            }
        }

        .disabled-page > {
            a, span {
                color: $color_primary50;
            }
        }

        .active-page > {
            a, span {
                z-index: 2;
                color: #FFF;
                background-color: $highlight_blue;
                border-color: transparent;
                cursor: default;
            }
        }
    }
}

.top-pagination-bar {
    margin: 11px 0 7px;
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
}

.bottom-pagination-bar {
    margin-top: 10px;
}

.alert {
    padding: 15px;
    margin-bottom: 20px;
    border: 1px solid transparent;
    border-radius: $widget_border_radius;
}

.alert-info {
    color: #31708f;
    background-color: #d9edf7;
    border-color: #bce8f1;
}

.alert-warning {
    color: #8a6d3b;
    background-color: #fcf8e3;
    border-color: #faebcc;
}

.alert-danger {
    color: #a94442;
    background-color: #f2dede;
    border-color: #ebccd1;
}

.alert-dismissable, .alert-dismissible {
    padding-right: 35px;
}

.alert-dismissable .close, .alert-dismissible .close {
    position: relative;
    top: -2px;
    right: -21px;
    color: inherit;
}

.close {
    float: right;
    font-size: 21px;
    font-weight: 700;
    line-height: 1;
    color: $color_primary100;
    filter: alpha(opacity=20);
    opacity: 0.2;
}

a.close {
    text-decoration: none !important;
    font-size: 18px !important;
    line-height: 1;

    &:hover {
        color: $color_primary100;
    }
}

.close {
    &:focus, &:hover {
        color: #000;
        text-decoration: none;
        cursor: pointer;
        filter: alpha(opacity=50);
        opacity: 0.5;
    }
}

.badge {
    min-width: 10px;
    padding: 0 7px;
    font-size: 12px;
    font-weight: 700;
    line-height: 1;
    color: #fff;
    text-align: center;
    white-space: nowrap;
    vertical-align: middle;
    background-color: #e84848;
    border-radius: 10px;
    box-sizing: border-box;
}

.form-submit-group {
    border-top: 1px solid rgba($color_primary100, 0.1);
    margin-top: 0.8em;
    padding-top: 0.5em;
    text-align: right;
}

.sidebox h3 {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    gap: 0.6rem;
    margin: 0;
    background: $color_navbar_bg;
    border-radius: 4px 4px 0 0;
    @if $is_light_theme {
        color: #fff;
    } 
    @else {
        color: #ccc;
    }
    padding: 0.55rem 0.75rem;
    line-height: 1.25;
    white-space: nowrap;
    font-size: 1.3em;
    overflow: hidden;
}

.sidebox h3 .fa {
    color: #ccc;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    float: none;
    margin: 0;
    width: 1.1em;
    height: 1.1em;
    line-height: 1;
    flex: 0 0 auto;
    overflow: visible;
}

.sidebox h3 .sidebox-count {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    min-width: 1.8em;
    height: 1.5em;
    padding: 0 0.4em;
    border-radius: 999px;
    font-size: 0.58em;
    line-height: 1;
    font-weight: 700;
    background: rgba($color_primary0, 0.18);
    color: $color_primary0;
    flex: 0 0 auto;
}

.sidebox-content {
    border: 1px solid $color_primary25;
    border-top: none;
    margin: 0;
    padding: 0.35rem 0.6rem 0.5rem;
    overflow: hidden;

    &.sidebox-table {
        border: none;
        padding: 0;

        .table {
            margin: 0 !important;
        }
    }
}

.sidebox {
    border-top-left-radius: $widget_border_radius;
    border-top-right-radius: $widget_border_radius;
    padding: 0 !important;
    padding-bottom: 1rem !important;
    overflow: hidden;
}

.ws-closed {
    position: sticky;
    top: 42px;
    background: $announcement_red;
    border-radius: 5px 5px 0 0;
    display: none;
}

.ws-closed a {
    display: block;
    padding: 7px 0;
    text-align: center;
    color: white;
    font-weight: 600;
}

.semibold {
    font-weight: 600;
}

.messages {
    list-style-type: none;
    padding: 0;

    li {
        padding: 1em 1.5em;
        margin-bottom: 1em;
        border: 1px solid transparent;
        border-radius: 5px;

        &.debug {
            color: #383d41;
            background-color: #e2e3e5;
            border-color: #d6d8db;
        }

        &.info {
            color: #0c5460;
            background-color: #d1ecf1;
            border-color: #bee5eb;
        }

        &.success {
            color: #155724;
            background-color: #d4edda;
            border-color: #c3e6cb;
        }

        &.warning {
            color: #856404;
            background-color: #fff3cd;
            border-color: #ffeeba;
        }

        &.error {
            color: #721c24;
            background-color: #f8d7da;
            border-color: #f5c6cb;
        }
    }
}

details {
    border: 1px solid $color_primary25;
    background: $color_primary5;
    padding: 5px 10px;
    border-radius: 4px;
}

// Design-system token layer (Phase 0).
//
// Emits the semantic design tokens from docs/design-system/03-design-tokens.md as
// CSS custom properties on :root. This partial is imported once by style.scss,
// after the theme `vars` file has defined `$is_light_theme`, so the light build
// (style.css) emits the light values and the dark build (dark/style.css) emits the
// dark values.
//
// The values below are the Warm Harvest (autumn) palette, the default theme (see
// docs/design-system/08-autumn-theme.md §3). Components migrate to `var(--...)` in
// later phases; the Summer palette keeps its own hardcoded values via the legacy
// $color_* SCSS vars.

@import "vars";

:root {
    // --- Color: surfaces & text ---
    @if $is_light_theme {
        --color-canvas: #fbf6ef;
        --color-surface: #ffffff;
        --color-surface-raised: #ffffff;
        --color-surface-alt: #f4ebdd;
        --color-border: #e4d5c1;
        --color-border-strong: #d3bfa4;
        --color-text: #2e241c;
        --color-text-secondary: #6e5d4e;
        --color-text-muted: #8a7360;
        --color-text-inverse: #ffffff;

        --color-accent: #c1440e;
        --color-accent-hover: #9e3609;
        --color-accent-contrast: #ffffff;
        --color-accent-2: #e0a82e;
        --color-navbar: #7a2906;

        --color-link: #1f5c6b;
        --color-link-hover: #c1440e;
        --color-focus-ring: #2c7a8c;

        --color-info-bg: #d9eef2;
        --color-info-fg: #1f5c6b;
        --color-success-bg: #ddf3e4;
        --color-success-fg: #177a3a;
        --color-warning-bg: #fff3cd;
        --color-warning-fg: #8a6100;
        --color-danger-bg: #f8dcdc;
        --color-danger-fg: #a52222;
    } @else {
        --color-canvas: #1a1512;
        --color-surface: #2e241c;
        --color-surface-raised: #4a3b2f;
        --color-surface-alt: #4a3b2f;
        --color-border: #4a3b2f;
        --color-border-strong: #6e5d4e;
        --color-text: #f4ebdd;
        --color-text-secondary: #a8907a;
        --color-text-muted: #8a7360;
        --color-text-inverse: #ffffff;

        --color-accent: #e07b39;
        --color-accent-hover: #f6cdb6;
        --color-accent-contrast: #120e0b;
        --color-accent-2: #e9c46a;
        --color-navbar: #120e0b;

        --color-link: #5fb3c4;
        --color-link-hover: #e9c46a;
        --color-focus-ring: #5fb3c4;

        --color-info-bg: #0d2b33;
        --color-info-fg: #5fb3c4;
        --color-success-bg: #0e3a22;
        --color-success-fg: #66ff88;
        --color-warning-bg: #3a2e05;
        --color-warning-fg: #ffdd66;
        --color-danger-bg: #3a1414;
        --color-danger-fg: #ff9999;
    }

    // --- Color: rating tiers ---
    @if $is_light_theme {
        --rating-none: #999999;
        --rating-newbie: #808080;
        --rating-pupil: #008000;
        --rating-specialist: #03a89e;
        --rating-expert: #0000ff;
        --rating-candidate-master: #aa00aa;
        --rating-master: #ff8c00;
        --rating-grandmaster: #ff0000;
    } @else {
        --rating-none: #aaaaaa;
        --rating-newbie: #988f81;
        --rating-pupil: #72ff72;
        --rating-specialist: #57fcf2;
        --rating-expert: #337dff;
        --rating-candidate-master: #ff55ff;
        --rating-master: #ff981a;
        --rating-grandmaster: #ff1a1a;
    }

    // --- Spacing (4px base) ---
    --space-0: 0;
    --space-1: 4px;
    --space-2: 8px;
    --space-3: 12px;
    --space-4: 16px;
    --space-5: 24px;
    --space-6: 32px;
    --space-7: 48px;
    --space-8: 64px;

    // --- Radius ---
    --radius-sm: 4px;
    --radius-md: 8px;
    --radius-lg: 12px;
    --radius-pill: 999px;

    // --- Elevation ---
    @if $is_light_theme {
        --shadow-0: none;
        --shadow-1: 0 1px 2px rgba(16, 24, 32, 0.08);
        --shadow-2: 0 2px 8px rgba(16, 24, 32, 0.1);
        --shadow-3: 0 8px 24px rgba(16, 24, 32, 0.14);
    } @else {
        --shadow-0: none;
        --shadow-1: 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
        --shadow-2: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55);
        --shadow-3: 0 8px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6);
    }

    // --- Typography ---
    --font-ui: "Inter", "Segoe UI", "Lucida Grande", Arial, sans-serif;
    --font-mono: "JetBrains Mono", "Fira Code", Consolas, "DejaVu Sans Mono", monospace;

    --text-xs: 12px;
    --text-sm: 13px;
    --text-base: 15px;
    --text-md: 17px;
    --text-lg: 20px;
    --text-xl: 24px;
    --text-2xl: 30px;

    --leading-xs: 1.4;
    --leading-sm: 1.45;
    --leading-base: 1.55;
    --leading-md: 1.5;
    --leading-lg: 1.4;
    --leading-xl: 1.3;
    --leading-2xl: 1.25;

    --weight-regular: 400;
    --weight-medium: 500;
    --weight-semibold: 600;
    --weight-bold: 700;

    // --- Motion ---
    --motion-fast: 120ms;
    --motion-base: 200ms;
    --motion-slow: 320ms;
    --ease-standard: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);

    // --- Z-index ---
    --z-base: 0;
    --z-dropdown: 1000;
    --z-navbar: 1000;
    --z-overlay: 1100;
    --z-modal: 1110;
    --z-toast: 1200;
}

```
